title: Review of c44's CIPS chemostat on fresh seed 2: washout every 800 t keeps the bodies dividing after the box fills (11 persistent splits after t=12000, generation 4) while the no-washout twin stops at t=11000; the population still drifts down (17 -> 13 -> 11)
summary: labkit runs of the chemostat world (20261026T1819-c44-cips-chemostat-sighting/world.py, 192^2, t=30000, noise 0.03) on seed 2 with wash_T 800 from t=12000 and with washout off. Washout: 21 persistent splits in all, 11 after t=12000, the last at t=27600, generation 4, 0 merges, bodies 17/13/11 at t=12000/21000/30000; dumbbells pinch through t=30000 (W800s2/sheet.png). No washout: 10 persistent splits, none after t=11000, generation 2, 17 bodies frozen from t=12000 to t=30000.

observations.finding: counts.txt: 11 births after t=12000 with washout vs 0 without; W800s2/sheet.png t=15600-28700 shows dumbbells pinching after the box has filled; population 17 -> 11 by t=30000, so births still lag removals (about 22 removals)

controls_run.finding: nowash_s2 (same world and seed, wash_T off): no persistent split after t=11000

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at wash_T 800 only; deaths are imposed by the washout rule, so only the births are the world's own, as the author states. The decline (17 -> 11) agrees with the finding that births replace about half of the removals.
